chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muthanna, from Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

If a man is detained (from completing the Hajj rites) and sends his sacrificial animal, but his head is affected (by hair regrowth or other impediment) before the animal is slaughtered, then he must slaughter a sheep in place of what he was detained from, or fast, or give charity to six poor people; and the fasting is three days, and the charity is half a Sa' for each poor person.

key_terms.إِحْصَار: Detention or prevention from completing Hajj rites
key_terms.صَاع: A traditional unit of volume for measuring food
key_terms.كَفَّارَة: Expiation or compensation for a missed/invalidated act
key_terms.هَدْي: Sacrificial animal sent by the pilgrim

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for a pilgrim detained before slaughtering their sacrificial animal?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Istibsar details the specific kaffarah for a pilgrim detained before slaughtering their sacrificial animal, offering three proportional alternatives: slaughtering a sheep, fasting three days, or feeding six poor people. The hadith reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on flexibility in expiation, allowing the pilgrim to choose the most feasible option based on their circumstances, while maintaining the spiritual balance of the Hajj rites.
